sections.title: Executive investment summary: a silver-contact converter priced as if a margin spike were permanent

blocks.text: Modison makes electrical contacts, the small metal parts inside switchgear that make and break a circuit. [F] (AR2026 p.145) It has one reported business segment, 'Manufacturing of Electrical Contacts'. [F] (AR2026 p.179) Its integrated chain runs from silver refining to contact materials to finished contacts. [F] (RATING) Low-voltage (LV) contacts are mostly silver and silver alloys (silver-cadmium-oxide, silver-tin-oxide, silver-nickel, silver-tungsten). High-voltage (HV) contacts are mostly copper and copper-tungsten arcing contacts and tulips for SF6 and gas-insulated switchgear. [MC] (CALL Oct 2022) [F] (PPT Mar 2024)

**The economics are a metal pass-through with a conversion margin on top.** Silver is ~75-80% of raw-material purchases. [F] (RATING) FY26 material cost net of inventory change was Rs 529.1 cr, or 74.5% of revenue from operations of Rs 710.3 cr. [E] (AR2026 p.142, p.166) Management says customer prices are indexed to silver at order booking or supply. However, 2-3 kg of silver must be held for every 1 kg shipped, and that residual stock carries the price risk. [MC] (CALL Oct 2022) Revenue and percentage margins therefore move with the silver price as well as with volume. [AI]

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. **Cash does not follow profit.** [F] CFO was -Rs 64 cr in FY26, -Rs 16 cr in FY25 and -Rs 4 cr in FY24, against PAT of Rs 73 cr, Rs 25 cr and Rs 21 cr. Three-year CFO/PAT is -0.71x and three-year FCF is -Rs 131 cr. (NUMBERS)

2. **The margin spike coincides with a large WIP build.** [F] Work-in-progress rose from Rs 107.96 cr to Rs 190.37 cr. The FY26 change in inventories credited to the P&L was Rs 89.86 cr. (AR2026 p.160, p.166) [MC] Management's own 2022 explanation of FY22 margin compression was the silver price falling on held stock (CALL Oct 2022). [AI] The FY26 expansion is plausibly the mirror image: holding gains on a larger silver-heavy inventory. It is not disclosed as such.

3. **Leverage has breached the rating agency's own downgrade marker.** [F] CARE lists overall gearing above 0.30x on a sustained basis as a negative trigger (RATING). FY26 debt/equity is 0.64x (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.79). Borrowings rose from Rs 73 cr to Rs 174 cr (NUMBERS).

4. **Valuation sits far above every DCF scenario.** [F] Bear/base/bull fair values are -Rs 45.5 / Rs 54.1 / Rs 143.1 per share vs a price of Rs 468. The reverse DCF finds no growth rate between -30% and +150% that justifies the EV at the model's margins. (NUMBERS)

5. **Related-party economics with promoter entities.** [F] FY26 purchases from promoter-controlled Modison Copper were Rs 42.29 cr and sales to it Rs 7.57 cr. The FY27 omnibus approval sought is Rs 80 cr. Royalty of Rs 0.69 cr went to a promoter partnership firm 'Modison'. (AR2026 p.29-30, p.174)

6. **Single-site concentration has already bitten.** [F] A fire at the factory on 7 Feb 2026 destroyed PPE and inventory: Rs 10.63 cr charged as exceptional. Only Rs 1.70 cr of insurance was confirmed; Rs 16.24 cr of claims are not yet admitted. (AR2026 p.188)

7. **Disclosure is thin and in places contradictory.** [F] The MD&A calls liquidity 'healthy' with 'robust operational cash flows' next to an operating cash flow of -Rs 64.18 cr (AR2026 p.79). No capacity, utilisation, volume, order book, LV/HV split or customer data is in the annual report. [F] (AR2026)
8. **Customer and supplier concentration.** [F] Top-5 customers ~45% of income; top-5 suppliers ~60-65% of purchases (RATING).

9. **Growth is price-inflated and export mix is shrinking.** [F] Outside-India revenue grew 9.2% vs 51.8% for India in FY26 (AR2026 p.179). [F] CARE attributed FY25 growth 'largely' to realisations from higher silver prices (RATING). [AI] Volume growth is not disclosed for FY25 or FY26.

10. **Executive pay is large relative to normal-year profit.** [F] The three promoter executive directors drew Rs 9.11 cr in FY26 (AR2026 p.100), against FY25 PAT of Rs 24.68 cr (AR2026 p.38). [E] That is ~12.6% of FY26 PAT and ~37% of FY25 PAT.

subsections.title: Key debates: where the market may be wrong, both ways

items: Is a 17-19% EBITDA margin the new normal? [MC] Management's 2022 'normalised' band was 12-14% (CALL Oct 2022). [F] FY23-FY25 delivered 7-9% (NUMBERS). [AI] The market prices near-current margins. Our DCF base uses 9%. The truth probably sits between, and it depends on silver.

Is revenue growth volume or price? [F] Revenue +44.9% in FY26 and +101.5% YoY in Q1 FY27 (NUMBERS). No volume disclosure exists after the FY22 figure of ~32 tonnes of silver [MC] (CALL Oct 2022). [AI] If most of the growth is silver price, it reverses when silver does.

Moat: monopoly or converter? [MC] The HV near-monopoly is plausible. [MC] LV share is only 16-17% against Choksi Heraeus, Hindustan Platinum and Modicon (CALL Oct 2022). [AI] Earlier 'monopolistic' framings in our own board notes overstate the position.

Is the balance-sheet stretch temporary? [AI] If silver stabilises, working capital should release cash and deleverage, which would be bullish. [F] The AGM sought a borrowing limit raised to Rs 500 cr for 'accelerating plans to expand its operations and scale up capacity' (AR2026 p.35), which points the other way.

Under-owned or under-scrutinised? [F] FIIs 0.92%, DIIs 0% (NUMBERS). [F] The exchange sought a clarification on price movement on 3 Sep 2026 (ANNOUNCEMENTS). [AI] Low institutional ownership can reflect neglect or a governance discount.

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus narrative, reflected in our own earlier board notes, is a hidden import-substitution monopoly re-rating on a structural grid cycle. Our reading of the filings is different. FY26 shows a silver-price-amplified earnings year with no cash conversion. The WIP build is large. Promoter-group related-party flows are material and growing. Leverage is above the rating agency's comfort threshold. Management has explained none of this in a public call. The HV franchise is real but is ~20% of sales [F] (RATING). The ~80% LV business is by management's own account single-digit margin and competitive [MC] (CALL Oct 2022). **The investment question is not growth but whether FY26 margins survive a flat or falling silver price, and the documents give no basis to assume they do.**

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and why

blocks.text: [MC] Management says LV is 'a low margin business in single digit' and HV 'a high margin business with high double digit' (CALL Oct 2022). [AI] With HV at ~20% of sales [F] (RATING), most profit in a normal year comes from HV conversion. The rest comes from how well the silver float is managed. In LV the customer effectively pays for the silver and Modison earns a fabrication fee. In a rising market the value of stock held above the invoiced silver creates gains; in a falling market it creates losses [MC] (CALL Oct 2022). [AI] That second source is not a franchise; it is a commodity position. CARE notes the company 'does not have a defined hedging policy' [F] (RATING). FY26 exceptional items include a hedging gain of Rs 2.61 cr vs a loss of Rs 1.70 cr in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.168).

[F] Fixed assets are light: net block of Rs 94 cr supported Rs 710 cr sales in FY26, a fixed-asset turnover of 7.55x (NUMBERS). [F] Working capital is heavy: inventories of Rs 219.80 cr and receivables of Rs 159.97 cr are 75.5% of total assets of Rs 502.75 cr (AR2026 p.141). [E] The business is asset-light in plant but capital-heavy in metal. Every rupee of revenue growth driven by silver price needs roughly a quarter to a half rupee of working capital (CCC 223 days FY26 [F] NUMBERS). Outsourced processing was Rs 6.95 cr [F] (AR2026 p.167). Related-party purchases from MCPL include 'job work services' [F] (AR2026 p.30).

blocks.text: [AI] Commodity-like: conventional LV silver contacts, bullion and cutlery. Price is silver plus a fabrication fee, there are several domestic competitors and ~35% of the LV market is imported [MC] (CALL Oct 2022). Differentiated: HV arcing contacts for GIS/AIS, where type-testing and a near-sole domestic position create switching costs [MC] (CALL Oct 2022). Emerging but unproven: AgSnO2, value-added sub-assemblies for L&T and GM Modular [MC] (CALL Oct 2022), and defence parts. R&D spend fell to Rs 1.59 cr in FY26 from Rs 2.11 cr in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.70), about 0.2% of revenue [E]. That is a modest base for a technology-led differentiation claim.

blocks.text: [AI] Modison is the only Indian supplier across LV, MV and HV contacts [MC] (CALL Oct 2022), with a defensible HV niche protected by expensive customer type-testing [MC]. Its blue-chip switchgear customers are riding a grid capex cycle [F] (RATING). TTM EBITDA of Rs 159 cr and PAT of Rs 102 cr [F] (NUMBERS) put it at 14.9x P/E, which is modest if the new margin regime holds. Promoters own 52% with no claimed pledges [F]/[MC], and CARE still rates it A with a Stable outlook [F] (RATING).

[AI] The margin step-up is five quarters old. It coincides with a silver-driven inventory build and has produced no operating cash, as CFO was negative for three years [F] (NUMBERS). Debt has more than doubled, and gearing is above CARE's own downgrade marker [F] (RATING). Related-party flows with promoter entities are growing [F] (AR2026 p.174).
